title: A keyless update retry after its commit can mint a new key and apply twice (a repeated block adds a second blocker)
outcome: A keyless update retry after its commit can mint a new key and apply twice (a repeated block adds a second blocker)
acceptance: Repeating a keyless update (block, revise, release and the other actions whose derived key binds the work or claim basis) after its first attempt committed replays the committed result instead of applying a second effect, or the word refuses the repeat with a typed answer naming how to read the committed outcome
Tests show a repeated keyless block after a lost answer leaves exactly one blocker, and a repeated keyless release does not fail as a fresh release against the released claim
